analysis.reason: The paper investigates double high-energy transients produced by black hole-star binary encounters with massive black holes, offering concrete accretion signatures and event rate predictions for nuclear transients.
analysis.result: The $\mu$TDE produces two accretion flares: a prompt fallback onto the stellar BH with peak rate $\approx 0.5\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{day}^{-1}$ (duration of hours to days) and a delayed slower return onto the MBH peaking at $\approx 50\,\mathrm{days}$ with a rate $\sim 3$ orders of magnitude lower. The dual-flare event rate is $\Gamma_{2\rm F} \approx 10^{-3}\Gamma_{\rm TDE} \approx 10^{-8}\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ at $M_\bullet = 10^6\,M_\odot$, and the time delay follows $\log_{10}(\Delta t_{\rm delay}/{\rm yr}) = 0.2511 - 0.1181X_M + 2.0696X_a + 0.0353X_M^2 + 0.1251X_a^2 - 0.1473X_M X_a$ with $X_M \equiv \log_{10}(M_\bullet/M_\odot)$ and $X_a \equiv \log_{10}(a_{\rm bin}/{\rm AU})$.
analysis.reading_entry: III.3 Double flares and time delay
analysis.problem: How tidal perturbations from an MBH on a stellar-mass black hole-star binary pump inner binary eccentricity to trigger a micro-TDE and subsequent dual-accretor flares.
analysis.method: High-precision few-body regularized chain scattering simulations using SpaceHub with up to 2.5PN corrections across grids of $M_\bullet$, $a_{\rm bin} \in [0.03, 30]\,\mathrm{AU}$, and $\tilde{v} \equiv v_\infty/v_{\rm orb}$, coupled with loss-cone flux integration ${\cal F}(r)=[{\cal F}_{\rm diff}^{-1}(r)+{\cal F}_{\rm full}^{-1}(r)]^{-1}$ where ${\cal F}_{\rm diff}\approx[\ln(2/\theta_{\rm lc})t_{r}]^{-1}$ and ${\cal F}_{\rm full}\approx\theta_{\rm lc}^{2}/t_{d}$.
citation_leads: II Numerical Methods: “Binary separation and exchange are identified when the energy of either binary member becomes negative”
III.3 Double flares and time delay: “The $\mu$TDE feeds two accretors: the $10\,M_{\odot}$ BH companion (prompt, fast mini-disk fallback) and the MBH”
III.4 Nuclear $mu$TDE rates: “We find that $\Gamma_{2\rm F}\approx 10^{-3}\Gamma_{\rm TDE}\approx 10^{-8}\,\rm yr^{-1}$ at $M_{\bullet}=10^{6}\,M_{\odot}$.”
analysis.research_progress: Establishes the branching ratios and ballistic debris partition of MBH-induced $\mu$TDEs, deriving the quantitative dual-flare time delay scaling and predicting a single-galaxy rate scaling as $\Gamma_{2\rm F} \propto (M_\bullet/10^8\,M_\odot)^{-(0.8\text{--}1.03)}$.

figures.caption: Figure 2: Snapshot of the spatial (left) and specific-energy (top right) distributions of the $10^{4}$ debris particles at $t=+260.58\,\rm days$ ($\approx 8.56\,\rm months$) after the $\mu$ TDE. The MBH sits at the center of the left panel (big black dot), and the stellar-mass BH companion (small black dot) is seen receding toward the right after its pericenter passage. The colorbar shows the specific energy of each debris particle normalized to the energy spread at the moment of disruption, $\Delta\varepsilon_{\rm frozen}\equiv GM_{\rm BH}R_{\star}/R_{t}^{2}$: blue for debris bound to the MBH ($\varepsilon_{\bullet} 0$). The zoomed-in inset in the left panel shows the debris orbital distribution and the mini-disk bound to the escaping BH. Finally, the lower right panel shows the fallback rates onto the BH and the MBH computed with the direct integration method (solid) and the frozen-in approximation (dashed). An animated version of this figure is available in the online article and at https://youtu.be/g8_UbibAqKQ. The 19 s animation follows the debris from the moment of disruption to $t=+260.58\,\rm days$, showing the formation of the mini-disk around the receding BH and the return of the MBH-bound debris.
figures.label: Fig. 2
figures.physical_core: Demonstrates the physical mechanism of the double-transient event: tidal perturbation induces a micro-TDE ($\mu$TDE) around the receding stellar-mass BH forming a bound mini-disk, while the remaining debris bound to the central MBH returns to produce a delayed secondary accretion flare, as quantified by the fallback rates onto both black holes.

figures.caption: Figure 3: Heat map of the time delay $\Delta t_{\rm delay}$ between the $\mu$ TDE and the peak fallback onto the perturber in the $a_{\rm bin}$ – $M_{\bullet}$ parameter space assuming the frozen-in approximation. Marginalization over $e_{\rm bin}$ and $v_{\infty}$ results in a median scatter of $\pm 0.67\,\rm dex$ about the values reported in the colorbar. There are no $\mu$ TDE outcomes in the top left gray region. The lower right magenta region corresponds to relativistic encounters for which the binary’s center of mass comes within $100\,R_{g}$ and our Newtonian integration scheme for the debris becomes inadequate.
figures.label: Fig. 3
figures.physical_core: Maps the theoretical parameter space of the time delay $\Delta t_{\rm delay}$ between the initial $\mu$TDE flare and the peak MBH fallback accretion flare across binary semi-major axis $a_{\rm bin}$ and MBH mass $M_\bullet$, delimiting the physical regimes of $\mu$TDE occurrence and relativistic boundaries.

analysis.reason: This work models polar shear ($s$) and interface ($i$) oscillation modes excited by neutron star crust elasticity, providing asteroseismic scaling relations to constrain nuclear incompressibility $K_0$ and symmetry energy slope $L$ relevant to resonant shattering precursors in compact binary mergers.
analysis.result: The radius-scaled shear mode frequencies $f_{s_i} R$ and mass-scaled interface mode frequencies $f_{i_i} M$ follow empirical universal relations parameterized by compactness $\chi \equiv (M/1.4M_\odot)/(R/12\ \mathrm{km})$, $K_0$, and $L$, largely independent of core equation of state stiffness. Spherical and cylindrical phases yield shear frequencies $f_s^{(\mathrm{SpCy})} \gtrsim 500\ \mathrm{Hz}$, while interface modes fall around $10-100\ \mathrm{Hz}$ with gravitational wave damping timescales $\tau_{\rm gw} \gtrsim 10^6\ \mathrm{s}$ for $s_1$ and $\tau_{\rm gw} > 10^8\ \mathrm{s}$ for $i_1$.
analysis.problem: Constraining uncertain nuclear matter parameters at saturation—namely incompressibility $K_0$ and symmetry energy slope $L$—using polar crustal oscillations ($s$- and $i$-modes) that penetrate into the stellar core, overcoming the limitation of torsional modes confined strictly to the crust.
analysis.method: Solves linear polar perturbations in a relativistic spherically symmetric metric $ds^{2}=-e^{2\Phi}dt^{2}+(1-2m(r)/r)^{-1}dr^{2}+r^{2}(d\theta^{2}+\sin^{2}\theta d\phi^{2})$ using the Cowling approximation $\delta(\nabla_{\mu}T^{\mu\nu})=0$. The crust employs the Oyamatsu-Iida EOS parameterized by $w=w_{0}+\frac{K_{0}}{2}u^{2}+[S_{0}+Lu]\delta^{2}$ with bcc lattice shear modulus $\mu_{\rm sp}=0.1194 n_{i}(Ze)^{2}/a$ and slab phase $\mu_{\rm sl}=0$, while the core uses a parameterized sound-speed EOS $p=\alpha(\varepsilon-\varepsilon_{t})+p_{t}$ with $\alpha=c_s^2$.
citation_leads: Elastic polar oscillations and nuclear parameters: “Owing to the elasticity of a neutron star, the shear and interface modes are excited”
2 Neutron star equilibrium and shear modulus: “That is, the crustal structure consists of two elastic regions separated by a fluid phase composed of slab-like nuclei”
3.1 Behavior of the $s$- and $i$-modes: “Both modes are excited by the elasticity inside the star. The number of $s$-modes is infinite, just like $p$-modes.”
3.3 Accuracy of the Cowling approximation: “the damping time to be $\gtrsim 10^{6}$ sec. for the $s_{1}$-modes and $>10^{8}$ sec. for the $i_{1}$-modes.”
Appendix B Dependence of the transition density between an elastic crust and the envelope.: “the $i_{2}$-mode frequencies decrease and eventually disappear when the transition density increases”
analysis.research_progress: Establishes universal asteroseismic relations linking global polar shear and interface mode frequencies ($f_{s_i} R$ and $f_{i_i} M$) to stellar compactness $\chi$ and nuclear saturation parameters ($K_0, L$) across diverse core stiffnesses, providing theoretical tools to interpret QPOs in precursor flares of short gamma-ray bursts.

analysis.reason: The paper reports phase-resolved X-ray polarimetry of the persistent black hole binary LMC X-1 with IXPE, detecting low-energy orbital modulation and enhanced polarization at inferior conjunction that constrains disk-outflow geometries.
analysis.result: Phase-resolved IXPE polarimetry reveals orbital modulation statistically preferred over a constant model in the $2\text{--}8\,\mathrm{keV}$ ($F=10.0, p=0.0004$) and $2\text{--}3\,\mathrm{keV}$ ($F=7.53, p=0.0016$) bands, despite an orbit-averaged polarization degree of $\mathrm{PD} = (0.8 \pm 0.4)\%$ below $\mathrm{MDP}_{99} = 1.2\%$. At inferior conjunction ($\\phi \in [-0.1, 0.1]$), polarization increases significantly to $\mathrm{PD} = (3.4 \pm 0.8)\%$ with $\mathrm{PA} = (50 \pm 7)^\circ$ in $2\text{--}8\,\mathrm{keV}$ and $\mathrm{PD} = (4.2 \pm 1.1)\%$ with $\mathrm{PA} = (46 \pm 8)^\circ$ in $2\text{--}3\,\mathrm{keV}$, aligned with the ionization cone and jet axis ($\sim 45^\circ$). Dilution analysis using $P = P_{\mathrm{disk}} \times (F_{\mathrm{disk}} / F_{\mathrm{total}})$ yields intrinsic disk polarization of $P_{\mathrm{disk}} = (4.6 \pm 1.3)\%$ at $2\text{--}3\,\mathrm{keV}$ and $(2.3 \pm 1.3)\%$ at $3\text{--}8\,\mathrm{keV}$.
analysis.problem: Standard electron scattering in an optically thick accretion disk atmosphere with inclination $i = (36.4 \pm 1.9)^\circ$ predicts $\mathrm{PD} \sim 1.3\%$ oriented perpendicular to the disk normal ($\\mathrm{PA} \sim 135^\circ$). This fails to explain the observed enhanced polarization degree $\mathrm{PD} \sim 4\%$ parallel to the disk normal and ionization cone ($\\mathrm{PA} \approx 46^\circ$) at inferior conjunction, as well as the significant orbital phase modulation.
analysis.method: Coordinated timing, spectral, and polarimetric data reduction of IXPE ($2\text{--}8\,\mathrm{keV}$, $\sim 562\,\mathrm{ks}$), NICER ($1\text{--}10\,\mathrm{keV}$, $\sim 25\,\mathrm{ks}$), and NuSTAR ($3\text{--}40\,\mathrm{keV}$, $\sim 19\,\mathrm{ks}$) folded at $P = 3.90917\,\mathrm{days}$. Stokes parameter variations were fitted using $(Q/I)(t) = A_Q \cos(2\pi(t/P + \phi_0)) + C_Q$ and $(U/I)(t) = A_U \cos(2\pi(t/P + \phi_0) - \pi) + C_U$. Instrument cross-calibration was handled via the $\mathrm{MBPO}$ broken power-law model, and spectro-polarimetry used $\mathrm{MBPO} \times \mathrm{TBABS} \times (\mathrm{KERRBB} + \mathrm{NTHCOMP} + \mathrm{GAUSS})$.
assumptions: The binary parameters are fixed to black hole mass $M_{\mathrm{BH}} = (10.9 \pm 1.4)\,M_\odot$, companion mass $(32 \pm 3)\,M_\odot$, and orbital inclination $i = (36.4 \pm 1.9)^\circ$.

analysis.reason: This paper presents 1D and 2D PIC simulations demonstrating that magnetic reconnection in shock-compressed Alfvén wave trains preferentially heats ions over electrons ($E_{\rm ele}/E_{\rm ion} \sim 0.4$), providing important microphysical constraints on collisionless shock energy partitioning.
analysis.result: In 2D parallel shocks, magnetic reconnection occurring in downstream compressed Alfvénic current sheets strongly heats ions, driving the electron-to-ion kinetic energy density ratio from $E_{\rm ele}/E_{\rm ion} \sim 0.7\text{--}0.9$ in 1D down to $E_{\rm ele}/E_{\rm ion} \sim 0.4$ ($E_{\rm ion}/E_0 \sim 2.8$ and $E_{\rm ele}/E_0 \sim 1.15$ for $u_0 = 0.4$). Preferential ion heating saturates when the transverse domain width exceeds $Y/(c/\omega_{\rm pi}) > 1.57$, whereas at low magnetization and high Mach numbers (e.g., $\sigma < 4\times 10^{-3}$ with $M_A \sim 5.9$ at $u_0 = 0.4$), reconnection heating becomes negligible and yields $E_e/E_i \sim 0.2\text{--}0.35$ in both 1D and 2D.

analysis.reason: This paper resolves a critical theoretical misconception regarding the Eddington luminosity of ultracompact stars ($R < 3M$) by accounting for photon back-reaction and calculates suppressed photon cooling timescales.
analysis.result: For ultracompact stars within the photon sphere ($R < 3M$), the inward momentum of returning photons raises the local photospheric critical luminosity to $L_{\rm crit} = \frac{L_{\rm Edd}}{(1 - 2M/R)^{1/2}\sin^2\delta} = \frac{L_{\rm Edd}R^2}{27M^2(1 - 2M/R)^{3/2}}$, exactly canceling the geometric escape cone factor $\sin^2\delta = 27\frac{M^2}{R^2}\left(1 - \frac{2M}{R}\right)$ and preserving the classical asymptotic critical luminosity $L_\infty = L_{\rm Edd}\left(1 - \frac{2M}{R}\right)^{1/2}$. Striped region indicates a vortex-free zone, with the rest of the container having a uniform distribution of vortices. Blue dashed arrow conveys the container’s direction of rotation. Blue and orange solid arrows specify the initial tangential flow and the effect of the sector, respectively. Purple arrowheads indicate the direction of flow on the contours of the vacated region due to the missing vortices. Left) Perturbation - A small sector near the boundary, of depth $d$ and opening angle $\phi$, is depleted of vortices, increasing the tangential flow at the tip. Right) Recapture - The sector is much larger than it was initially, now described by a depth $d^{*}$ and an opening angle $\phi^{*}$. analysis.result: Pure disk drag imposes a minimum period $P_{\min} \propto M_{\rm BH}$ due to stripping-induced stellar destruction ($f_{\rm ml} \approx 6 \times 10^{-4}$), while adding GW orbital decay allows stars to access sub-day periods across black hole masses ($t_{\rm GW} / t_{\rm drag} \propto M_{\rm BH}^{-11/6} r_p^{3/2} a^0$). Standard EMRI formation criteria comparing $t_{\rm GW}$ and $t_{L,\rm rel}$ fail because stars near $r_{p,\min}$ disrupt on a much shorter local timescale $t_{\rm TDE} = \frac{(L - L_{\min})^2}{L_c^2(a)} t_{\rm 2B,rel} \ll t_{L,\rm rel}$, but TDE disk gas drag boosts the QPE orbital survival fraction from $f_{\rm QPE,\max} \lesssim 5\text{--}10\%$ up to $\sim 30\%$ under fiducial parameters ($M_{\rm BH} = 10^6\,M_\odot$, $h=0.1$, $\Gamma_{\rm TDE} = 10^{-4}\,{\rm yr^{-1}}$, $t_{\rm 2B,rel} = 10\,{\rm Gyr}$).

analysis.reason: The paper develops an orbital remapping scintillometry technique for the Galactic binary pulsar PSR J0737$-$3039A/B to constrain distance and ISM scattering screens for tests of general relativity, bearing no substantive connection to high-energy transients, FRB/PRS, supernovae, or relativistic jets.
analysis.result: The orbital remapping fit determines a scaled curvature $\nu\sqrt{\eta_y} = 0.2066\pm 0.0025\mathrm{\,GHz\,\mu s^{1/2}}$, orbital amplitude $A_{\rm orb} = 211\pm 9\mathrm{\,Mm}$, screen orientation $\xi = 73.1^\circ\pm 2.6^\circ$, and phase offset $\delta = 0.24^\circ\pm 0.75^\circ$. Under uniform priors, the primary screen yields effective distance $d_{\rm eff} = 418^{+40}_{-37}\mathrm{\,pc}$, pulsar distance $d_p = 781^{+62}_{-94}\mathrm{\,pc}$ ($786^{+48}_{-55}\mathrm{\,pc}$ with VLBI prior), screen distance $d_s = 270^{+24}_{-23}\mathrm{\,pc}$, and fractional distance $s_1 = 0.65^{+0.02}_{-0.03}$; the second screen gives $\sqrt{(1-s_2)/s_2}|\cos\Delta\Omega_2| = 1.56$ with $d_{s2} \ge 547\mathrm{\,pc}$.
analysis.problem: Measuring the moment of inertia $I_A$ to $\sim 20\%$ to test the neutron star equation of state requires constraining $\dot{P}_B$ kinematic terms to $0.01\mathrm{\,fs/s}$, necessitating distance accuracy $\lesssim 10\%$, but current timing ($465^{+134}_{-85}\mathrm{\,pc}$) and VLBI ($770\pm 70\mathrm{\,pc}$) distances are in tension; furthermore, rapid orbital velocity changes disrupt parabolic scintillation arcs.
analysis.method: An orbital remapping framework decomposes effective displacement along a 1D screen $r_{\rm eff,\parallel}(t) = v_{\rm eff,sys,\parallel}t - A_{\rm orb}f(\phi-\omega)\cos(\phi+\delta)$ and normalizes it to $y(t) = r_{\rm eff,\parallel}(t)/A_{\rm orb} = V_y \frac{t}{a/v_p} - f(\phi-\omega)\cos(\phi+\delta)$ to recover parabolic arcs $f_\nu = \eta_y f_y^2$ with $\eta_y = \frac{\lambda_0^2 d_{\rm eff}}{2c A_{\rm orb}^2}$; MCMC sampling and forward numerical modeling of double scattering via `screens` constrain screen and orbital parameters from MeerKAT and GBT dynamic spectra.
assumptions: The scintillation is dominated by one nearly one-dimensional scattering screen.
limits: Discarding phase information in secondary spectra limits the sensitivity to phase offset $\delta$, requiring $\sigma_\delta \simeq 1/(10|\tan i_p|)\mathrm{\,rad} \simeq 0.06^\circ$ to reach a $10\%$ distance precision.

figures.caption: Figure 3: Sketch of the geometry. The left-most plane shows the motion of pulsar A on the sky, at a distance $d_{p}$, as seen from the solar system barycenter, with its trajectory during an observation shown as the solid line. Radiation from the pulsar can follow multiple paths to reach the observer: directly, via the line of sight, indicated by the black line, and indirectly, scattered by one or more scattering screens, with examples of single-scattered rays shown with the yellow and blue lines. The two middle planes each represent a scattering screen, at distance $d_{s}$. The scattering is assumed to be due to highly anisotropic density gradients, indicated by the bands, so that light can be bent in only one direction. This results in sets of scattering points which are on a line perpendicular to the bands, at orientation $\xi$, and which may move with velocity $v_{s}$ along that direction (the other direction is not measurable). The right-most plane shows the motion of the Earth around the Sun, as projected on the plane perpendicular to the line of sight. The latin numerals mark four times, for each of which a panel in the bottom shows the effective pulsar position, as projected on each of the two screens. One sees that the amplitude of the projected orbital motion is similar for the two screens: while screen 2 is closer to the pulsar than screen 1, which leads to larger projected motion, it is also less aligned, which reduces it. The annual variation, however, is much larger for the first screen, because Earth’s motion is aligned much better with it.
figures.label: Fig. 3
figures.physical_core: Schematic representation of the multi-screen scattering geometry along the line of sight to PSR J0737-3039A at distance $d_p$. It illustrates the direct line of sight and single-scattered ray paths traversing two anisotropic interstellar plasma screens at distances $d_s$ (characterized by orientation angle $\xi$ and transverse velocity $v_s$), Earth's projected orbital motion, and the effective pulsar orbital trajectory projected onto each screen across four key orbital phases.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Constraining orbital parameters by requiring similar Doppler-delay spectra. Top: The observed dynamic spectrum for a selected frequency range of an S-band observation. One sees clear pattern reversals around the black lines, which mark the turning points inferred from the model fits from Section V (see Figures 3 and 4 for the geometry). The faint vertical stripes are due to eclipses by pulsar B, at $\sim\!0.25$ and $2.70{\rm\,h}$, and periods of strong RFI. Middle: The same spectrum resampled to effective position projected on the screen for each of the three regions separated by the turning points, again using the fits from Section V. To help keep the time order the same, the direction in which effective position is displayed is changed around the turning points. Bottom: Delay-Doppler spectra for each of the three regions. The three power spectra are very similar, each having clearly defined arcs with the same discrete substructures. The stronger power at the top of the arc at negative- $f_{y}$ reflects the fine striations seen in the dynamic spectra.
figures.label: Fig. 1
figures.physical_core: Observational demonstration of the orbital resampling method applied to an S-band observation of PSR J0737-3039A. It displays the observed dynamic spectrum exhibiting scintillation pattern reversals at orbital turning points, the dynamic spectrum resampled to effective projected position on the principal screen, and the recovered Doppler-delay ($f_y, \tau$) secondary spectra showing crisp, consistent scintillation arcs across all three orbital regions.

analysis.reason: This work presents long-term full GRMHD simulations of circumbinary disk accretion onto a supermassive binary black hole, discovering a Dual Horizon-MAD regime with periodic accretion and jet emissions directly relevant to compact object high-energy observations.
analysis.result: The binary reaches a Dual Horizon-MAD (DH-MAD) state where the dimensionless horizon flux saturates at $\phi_{\rm BH} \sim 20$ after $\sim 23$ orbits, launching relativistic jets with average Poynting luminosity $L_{\rm Poyn}/\dot{M} = 0.01$ (efficiency $\eta = 1\%$). Individual BH accretion rates show dominant periodicity at $f \sim 0.9f_{\rm orb}$ (with secondary peaks at $f \sim 1.8f_{\rm orb}$), while total accretion modulates at $f \sim 1.8f_{\rm orb}$ and dimensionless horizon magnetic flux oscillates at $f \sim 0.4f_{\rm orb}$.
analysis.problem: Investigating long-term circumbinary disk accretion and magnetic flux accumulation in equal-mass binary black holes in full general relativity to determine cavity magnetic structure, minidisk survival, and multi-messenger electromagnetic signatures.
analysis.method: 3D full GRMHD simulations using the Einstein Toolkit with LeanBSSN for dynamical spacetime and IllinoisGRMHD for magnetohydrodynamics, modeling an equal-mass ($q=1$), non-spinning ($\chi_1=\chi_2=0$) binary at initial separation $d/M=30$ with circumbinary poloidal magnetic field ($\beta_{\rm ini}=52.42$) evolved past $t \simeq 52,000\,GM/c^3$.

Statistically significant positive correlations ($2.1\sigma - 3.4\sigma$) are discovered between rest-frame RM dispersion $\sigma_{\mathrm{RM,host}} = \sigma_{\mathrm{RM}}(1+z)^2$, host Faraday rotation $|\mathrm{RM}_{\mathrm{host}}|$, and host scattering timescale $	au_{\mathrm{host}}$ assuming $	au \propto

u)=(L/I)_{\mathrm{int}}\exp(-2c^4
u^{-4}\sigma_{\mathrm{RM}}^2)$; and (3) A combined birefringence and depolarization model incorporating high-frequency orthogonal mode mixing with a transition frequency $
u_c$ and spectral index $\alpha$.
assumptions: Depolarization is driven by Gaussian fluctuations in the Faraday dispersion of intervening magnetoionic media: $(L/I)(\nu) = (L/I)_{\mathrm{int}} \exp\left(-2c^4\nu^{-4}\sigma_{\mathrm{RM}}^2\right)$.

analysis.reason: This paper presents the benchmark population synthesis and joint parameter constraints for fast radio bursts using 1,683 events from the Second CHIME/FRB Catalog with rigorous injection-based selection effect corrections. It establishes that cataclysmic compact binary mergers cannot dominate the local non-repeating FRB population due to their much lower rates, whereas core-collapse supernovae remain viable.
analysis.result: The local volumetric rate density of FRBs at $z=0$ above pivot energy $E_{\rm pivot} = 10^{39}\,\mathrm{erg}$ (with scattering time $\tau < 30\,\mathrm{ms}$ at $600\,\mathrm{MHz}$) is $\Phi_0 = 1.1^{+0.4}_{-0.3} \times 10^5\,\mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$. The energy distribution, modeled by a Schechter function assuming isotropic emission over a $1\,\mathrm{GHz}$ bandwidth, yields a differential power-law slope $\gamma = -1.41^{+0.27}_{-0.21}\,(\mathrm{stat.}) \pm 0.35\,(\mathrm{sys.})$ and cutoff energy $E_{\rm char} = 2.0^{+2.6}_{-1.0}\,(\mathrm{stat.}) \pm 0.5\,(\mathrm{sys.}) \times 10^{41}\,\mathrm{erg}$. Cosmic rate evolution parameterized as $(1+z)^n$ yields $n = 0.5^{+0.4}_{-0.4}$, consistent at $2\sigma$ with both no evolution ($n=0$) and SFR-tracing ($n=1$). The mean spectral index is $\alpha = -1.0^{+0.5}_{-0.6}$ ($F \propto \nu^{\alpha}$), rejecting a flat spectrum at $>2\sigma$. The rest-frame host galaxy dispersion measure follows a log-normal distribution with median $\mathrm{DM}_{\rm host, med}^\prime = 199^{+34}_{-36}\,(\mathrm{stat.}) \pm 50\,(\mathrm{sys.})\,\mathrm{pc\,cm}^{-3}$ and standard deviation $\sigma_{\rm host} = 285^{+72}_{-86}\,(\mathrm{stat.}) \pm 71\,(\mathrm{sys.})\,\mathrm{pc\,cm}^{-3}$.
analysis.problem: Simultaneously determining the intrinsic cosmological rate density, energy function, spectral index, and host galaxy DM distribution of FRBs while correcting for complex telescope and pipeline selection biases, and resolving the origin of a significant $>3\sigma$ model underprediction of bright, low-DM bursts in the region $\mathcal{R} = \{(\mathrm{DM}, \mathrm{S/N}): \mathrm{DM} < 800\,\mathrm{pc\,cm}^{-3}, \mathrm{S/N} > 40\}$.
analysis.method: Constructed a forward population synthesis model evaluating the joint distribution $R(F, \mathrm{DM} \mid \boldsymbol{\lambda}) = \int dz\, R(F, z)\, P(\mathrm{DM} \mid z)$ fitted to 1,683 bursts selected from CHIME/FRB Catalog 2 (using real-time detection $\mathrm{S/N} > 12$ as flux proxy and keeping only first bursts for repeaters). Selection effects were empirically calibrated using a $\sim 100\times$ enlarged injection simulation dataset extending scattering timescales up to $\tau \le 30\,\mathrm{ms}$. Evaluated Poisson deviance on a $15 \times 10$ log-grid of $(\mathrm{S/N}, \mathrm{DM})$, determined global MLE via Differential Evolution, and performed 7-parameter MCMC posterior sampling via `emcee` (60 walkers) achieving convergence with $\hat{R} < 1.01$ and $\mathrm{ESS} > 1900$.
assumptions: FRBs are drawn from a single homogeneous population where repeating and non-repeating sources share the same underlying energy distribution.
limits: The best-fit model underpredicts the bright, low-DM subpopulation ($\\mathcal{R}$ region), which accounts for $\sim 60\%$ of total Poisson deviance despite comprising only $\sim 15\%$ of sample counts.

II.1 The Second CHIME/FRB Catalog: “The second CHIME/FRB catalog contains 4539 bursts from 3641 unique sources”
V Results: “All parameters yielded $\hat{R}<1.01$, indicating excellent mixing across chains.”
V.1 Goodness of fit: “it accounts for $\sim 60\%$ of the total Poisson deviance.”
VI.1 FRB Volumetric Rate: “compact object mergers, do not dominate the local non-repeating FRB population”
VI.4 FRB Spectral Index: “The parameter $\alpha$ represents the average FRB spectral index, defined as $F\propto\nu^{\alpha}$”
Appendix A Supplemental Results for Extended Population Model: “all channels share the base model’s energy function and differ only in their DTDs and weights $f_{i}$.”
analysis.research_progress: Expands population modeling to the Second CHIME/FRB Catalog with 1,683 bursts and an updated $30\,\mathrm{ms}$ injection calibration, halving statistical uncertainties relative to Catalog 1; establishes a local rate $\Phi_0 = 1.1^{+0.4}_{-0.3} \times 10^5\,\mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ that rules out cataclysmic compact object mergers as dominant progenitors while matching core-collapse supernova rates; confirms a steep spectral index $\alpha = -1.0^{+0.5}_{-0.6}$ disfavoring flat emission at $>2\sigma$; and refines the rest-frame host DM median to $199^{+34}_{-36}\,\mathrm{pc\,cm}^{-3}$.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Corner plot of the MCMC posterior distributions corresponding to the $R(F,{\rm DM})$ model described in § III. We apply a thinning factor of 20 for visual clarity. Parameters $\Phi_{0}$, $E_{\rm char}$, $\mu_{{\rm host},10}$, and $\sigma_{{\rm host},10}$ are fit in natural-log space but presented here in common logarithm for ease of interpretation. The solid vertical lines represent the median of the one-dimensional distributions, while dashed lines enclose the $68\%$ credible intervals. The two-dimensional contours represent the $1\sigma$, $1.5\sigma$, and $2\sigma$ confidence levels. Systematic uncertainties evaluated in § V are not plotted here.
figures.label: Fig. 1
figures.physical_core: MCMC posterior probability distributions constraining key cosmological FRB population parameters, including the local volumetric rate $\Phi_{0}$, characteristic maximum energy $E_{\rm char}$, and host-galaxy dispersion measure distribution parameters $\mu_{{\rm host},10}$ and $\sigma_{{\rm host},10}$.

figures.caption: Figure 2: Comparison of the observed $\rm{S/N}\text{--}\rm{DM}$ distribution with the best-fit model predictions. The right panel shows the absolute values of the Poisson deviation as defined in Equation 5. The two distributions are largely consistent within $3\sigma$, with the notable exception of the low-DM, high- S/N regime where the observed counts systematically exceed model predictions. A hint of this feature can be made out visually in Figure 3 of S23; however, it is less apparent due to lower bin counts.
figures.label: Fig. 2
figures.physical_core: Two-dimensional comparison of observed CHIME/FRB Catalog 2 burst counts against best-fit population model predictions in the $\rm{S/N}\text{--}\rm{DM}$ plane alongside Poisson deviance residuals, highlighting a significant systematic excess of observed high-S/N bursts at low DM.

analysis.reason: The paper investigates the propagation dynamics, recollimation shocks, and lateral stability of extraordinary relativistic jets on multi-Mpc scales using 3D RMHD simulations, directly relevant to relativistic jets and compact object outflows.
analysis.result: In underdense void environments (Case A), relativistic jets with injection Lorentz factor $\Gamma = 12$ accelerate to $\Gamma > 20$ via recollimation shocks, maintaining an average propagation speed $v_{\rm head} \sim 0.72c$ and reaching a total scale of $\sim 9\ \mathrm{Mpc}$ in $t \approx 19.6\ \mathrm{Myr}$ with an aspect ratio of $\sim 20$ and energy $E_{\rm inj} \approx 0.9 \times 10^{62}\ \mathrm{erg}$. In cluster media (Cases B and C), jets stall at $\sim 1.5\text{--}2\ \mathrm{Mpc}$ ($E_{\rm inj} \sim [1.2, 3.4] \times 10^{62}\ \mathrm{erg}$ at $[26.1, 76.6]\ \mathrm{Myr}$). High relativistic thrust at $\Gamma \ge 12$ strongly suppresses Kelvin-Helmholtz and kink instabilities (FFT fluctuation power $\sum |F(k)|^2 / N \lesssim 10^{-2}$ at $\lesssim 3\ \mathrm{Mpc}$), preventing lateral disruption until the jet head.
analysis.problem: Understanding the physical survival mechanisms and observational scarcity of multi-Mpc giant radio galaxies (GRGs, such as Porphyrion spanning $\sim 7\ \mathrm{Mpc}$), particularly whether their terminal reach is constrained by destructive MHD instabilities, ambient density gradients, or central engine lifetimes.
analysis.method: 3D relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (RMHD) simulations using the GPU-accelerated code `gPLUTO` with the Taub–Matthews equation of state. Jets are injected with power $P_{\rm jet} = 3.5 \times 10^{46}\ \mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}$, bulk Lorentz factor $\Gamma = 12$, density $\rho_j = 5 \times 10^{-8}\ \mathrm{amu\ cm^{-3}}$, magnetization $\sigma = B_j^2 / (4\pi \Gamma^2 \rho_j h_j) = 0.1$, and nozzle radius $r_j = 2\ \mathrm{kpc}$. Synchrotron emissivity $\mathcal{I}'_{\rm syn}$ at $144\ \mathrm{MHz}$ is modeled assuming non-thermal electron energy density fraction $\epsilon = 0.5$, power-law index $p = 2.2$ over $10^2 \le \gamma \le 10^6$, and Doppler beaming factor $\mathcal{D}$. Ambient gas is set via a King $\beta$-profile ($\rho_c = 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{amu\ cm^{-3}}$, $r_c = 33\ \mathrm{kpc}$, $\beta = 0.55$, $kT \sim 1.1\ \mathrm{keV}$).

3.4. Evolution of the jet(s): “The first recollimation shock is particularly strong, producing significant compression of the jet plasma”
4.2. Understanding the scarcity of such extreme radio galaxies: “From a dynamical perspective, only suficiently powerful jets are capable of sustaining long-range propagation”

analysis.research_progress: Establishes that relativistic jets have no strict physical upper limit in length when propagating through underdense voids, achieving multi-Mpc lengths at $v_{\rm head} \sim 0.72c$ because relativistic inertia suppresses destructive lateral instabilities. analysis.reason: AT 2024qfm is the most X-ray luminous LFBOT observed at early times ($L_{\rm x} \approx 10^{44}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$), providing critical observational constraints on central engine driving, high-energy reprocessing efficiency, and relativistic shock-CSM interaction.
analysis.result: AT 2024qfm reaches an unprecedented early peak X-ray luminosity of $L_{\rm x} \approx 10^{44}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ at $\delta t < 20\,\mathrm{days}$, showing a steep initial decay $\propto t^{-6}$ followed by rebrightening and spectral hardening. The source transitions to $L_{\rm x} \approx L_{\rm opt}$ as early as $\delta t \approx 7\,\mathrm{days}$ (reaching $L_{\rm x}/L_{\rm opt} \approx 8.4$ at $\delta t \approx 14\,\mathrm{days}$), requiring an equatorial slow-outflow fraction $\phi_0 \lesssim 0.1$ with Thomson optical depth $\tau_{\rm T} < 1$ at $\delta t \approx 9\,\mathrm{days}$. Its X-ray spectrum is notably hard ($F_\nu \propto \nu^{-\beta}$ with $\beta \approx 0.5$ vs $\beta \approx 1$ in GRBs), and late-time radio emission reveals an outflow of roughly constant velocity $v \approx 0.1c$ entering an order-of-magnitude denser CSM.
analysis.reading_entry: VIII.2 Linking X-rays with Optical emission in LFBOTs
analysis.problem: Elucidating the physical mechanisms powering luminous fast blue optical transients (LFBOTs), specifically whether the optical emission is produced by reprocessing of central engine high-energy emission and how the fast-moving ejecta interact with dense circumstellar media.
analysis.method: Multi-wavelength synthesis combining Swift (XRT/UVOT), NuSTAR, CXO, NICER, NOEMA, and JVLA data. Radio spectra are modeled using fast-cooling synchrotron self-absorption (SSA) with electron energy index $p=3$, yielding scaling relations $R = 7.7570\times 10^{15}\,f_{\rm eB}^{-1/13}(f/0.5)^{-1/13}(F_{\rm pk}/\mathrm{Jy})^{6/13}(D/\mathrm{Mpc})^{12/13}(\nu_{\rm pk}/5\,\mathrm{GHz})^{-11/13}(t/100\,\mathrm{days})^{1/13}\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $B = 0.3545\,f_{\rm eB}^{-4/13}(f/0.5)^{-4/13}(F_{\rm pk}/\mathrm{Jy})^{-2/13}(D/\mathrm{Mpc})^{-4/13}(\nu_{\rm pk}/5\,\mathrm{GHz})^{21/13}(t/100\,\mathrm{days})^{4/13}\,\mathrm{G}$. UV/optical data are modeled via expanding blackbody photospheres ($T_{\rm BB} \approx 1.1\text{--}1.65\times 10^4\,\mathrm{K}$, $v_{\rm phot} \approx 0.02\text{--}0.05c$).
assumptions: Radio emission arises from synchrotron self-absorption in the fast-cooling regime under microphysical equipartition ($\epsilon_{\rm e} = \epsilon_{\rm B} = 0.3$) and electron power-law index $p=3$.
limits: Reconciling the observed high X-ray to optical luminosity ratio requires an equatorial slow reprocessor covering fraction $\phi_0 \lesssim 0.1$, ruling out conventional quasi-spherical models ($\phi_0 = 0.5$).
citation_leads: I Introduction: “Radio emission from LFBOTs is understood to be synchrotron radiation produced by the interaction of fast-moving ejecta”
III.1 Swift-UVOT (UV) and optical photometry: “We reduced and analyzed the UVOT data following standard practice as described in [[47](#bib.bib47)]”
VII.3.2 A separate outflow component: “outflow of roughly constant velocity of $\approx 0.1$c moving to an environment that is an order of magnitude denser”
VIII.2.1 External reprocessor: “Reproducing the observed luminosities requires $\phi_{\rm 0}\lesssim 0.1$.”
VIII.3 X-ray properties: “LFBOTs have a typical $\beta\approx 0.5$, while GRB X-ray afterglows are characterized by $\beta\approx 1$.”
Appendix A Synchrotron self-absorption model: “For $p=3$, $c_{5}=7.51952\times 10^{-24}$ and $c_{6}=7.95999\times 10^{-41}$ (in cgs units)”
analysis.research_progress: Establishes AT 2024qfm as the most X-ray luminous LFBOT at early times ($L_{\rm x} \approx 10^{44}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$), shows that LFBOT X-ray spectra are systematically harder ($\beta \approx 0.5$) than GRB afterglows ($\beta \approx 1$), and reveals that early high-energy transparency is reached far faster than in AT 2018cow ($L_{\rm x} \approx L_{\rm opt}$ at $\approx 7\,\mathrm{d}$ vs $\approx 20\,\mathrm{d}$) due to an inefficient, low-covering-fraction reprocessor ($\phi_0 \lesssim 0.1$).

figures.caption: Figure 12: Left panel: Radio light curve of AT 2024qfm at X-band (8–12 GHz) in the context of other LFBOTs (star symbols) and energetic transients including GRBs, Supernovae, and TDEs [ 50, 57, and references therein]. All LFBOTs peak at similar times ($\delta t_{\rm rest}\approx 50-100$ days) in the X-band, with peak luminosities spanning only a factor of $\approx 10$. Right panel: The mm-band (80–200 GHz) light curves of AT 2024qfm along with other mm-bright LFBOTs (star symbols); AT 2018cow [ 41 ], AT2020xnd [ 37 ], AT 2022tsd [ 38 ], AT 2023fhn [ 34 ], and AT 2024wpp [ 57 ]. All mm-bright LFBOTs peak at $\delta t_{\rm rest}\approx 1$ month, with a larger dispersion of $\approx 100$ in peak luminosity. Other extragalactic mm-bright transients are also shown for comparison [ 20, and references therein].
figures.label: Fig. 12
figures.physical_core: Comparison of AT 2024qfm radio (X-band, 8–12 GHz) and mm-band (80–200 GHz) light curves against known LFBOTs and other energetic transients (GRBs, SNe, TDEs). It illustrates that all LFBOTs peak at $\delta t_{\rm rest} \approx 50-100$ days in the X-band with peak luminosities spanning a factor of $\approx 10$, whereas mm-bright LFBOTs peak earlier at $\delta t_{\rm rest} \approx 1$ month with a wider luminosity dispersion of $\approx 100$, where AT 2024qfm is the least luminous at mm wavelengths.

analysis.reason: The paper investigates the hydrodynamics of tertiary mass transfer and Roche-lobe overflow in hierarchical triple star systems, lacking substantive connection to the group's core interests in FRB/PRS environments, supernova central engines, shock breakouts, relativistic jets, or compact object high-energy observations.
analysis.result: Tertiary mass transfer exhibits quasi-periodic modulation matching donor eigenmodes ($T \approx 2.6$ and $T \approx 3.4$ in units of $(G^{-1}M_d^{-1}R_d^3)^{1/2}$), with time-averaged mass loss scaling as $\langle\dot{M}_d\rangle \propto \langle\dot{M}_{d,0}\rangle (1 + C a_b^{6.1 \pm 0.9})$ due to the inner binary quadrupole perturbation $\delta\Phi_2 \propto a_b^2$. For tight binaries ($a_b = 0.3 R_d$), gas circularizes into a circumbinary disk with cavity radius $a_{\rm cav} \approx 1.68 a_b$ governed by Lindblad resonance at $r_{\rm LR} = 1.31 a_b$, whereas wide binaries ($a_b = 1.0 R_d$) disrupt disk formation and drive spiral outflows.
analysis.reading_entry: IV.3 Time-dependent mass transfer & forced donor oscillations
analysis.problem: How the finite orbital separation $a_b$ and time-variable gravitational potential of an inner binary modulate tertiary Roche-lobe overflow, excite donor stellar oscillations, and dictate the transition between circumbinary disk accretion and global mass ejection.
analysis.method: Three-dimensional compressible hydrodynamic simulations using Athena++ in spherical coordinates with a static self-gravity formulation $\boldsymbol{\alpha}_{\rm sg} \approx -\frac{G[M_{\rm enc,d}(r)-M_d]}{|\mathbf{r}|^3}\mathbf{r}$, parameterized cooling $t_{\rm cool}=(t_{\rm max}-t_{\rm min})\tanh[(\rho/\rho_c)^\xi]+t_{\rm min}$ targeting $h=H/R=0.2$, and stellar pulsation eigenmode identification with GYRE.
assumptions: The tertiary donor star is initialized as a hydrostatic polytrope with $\Gamma_s = \gamma = 5/3$ under a static self-gravity approximation.
limits: Restricted to coplanar circular orbits ($e=0$), equal-mass inner binaries ($m_1=m_2$), and mass transfer regimes where cumulative envelope loss is $\lesssim 10^{-3} M_d$.
citation_leads: Time-variable tertiary mass transfer in hierarchical triple systems: “we study tertiary mass transfer in hierarchical triple systems using three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations.”
II.5 Point-Mass and Perturbative Limits: “the odd multipoles vanish by symmetry, leaving the quadrupole as the leading finite-separation correction,”
III.3 Source terms: “We treat this acceleration in an approximate way by using a “static self-gravity” approach”
IV.1 Time-dependent Roche geometry: “causing the Roche lobes of the donor and accretor to come in and out of contact.”
IV.3 Time-dependent mass transfer & forced donor oscillations: “The orbit of the inner binary transfers angular momentum to the gas, exciting the material and allowing it to escape.”
IV.6 Outflows and global morphology: “Compact inner binaries retain much of the transferred material in a circumbinary structure”

analysis.research_progress: Demonstrated that finite binary separation drives a non-linear scaling of orbit-averaged mass loss $\langle\dot{M}_d\rangle \propto a_b^{2n+3}$ for polytropic index $n=3/2$ through quadrupole tidal forcing, exciting both radial and non-radial donor eigenmodes.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Schematic representation for the setup of our system of interest. Top: Spatial representation of the numerical setup of the system. The tertiary polytropic star is placed at the center of the coordinate system with a point mass as a core. The inner binary is placed in the $x-y$ plane. Both the orbit of the inner binary and the orbit of the tertiary are initiated in the same $x-y$ plane. The simulations take place in a spherical-polar coordinate grid with $[r,\varphi,\theta].$ Bottom: Slice taken for $z=0$. The masses and length scales of the system are defined.
figures.label: Fig. 1
figures.physical_core: Spatial and geometric setup of the hierarchical triple system in spherical-polar coordinates $[r, \varphi, \theta]$, showing the central polytropic donor star with core point mass in the orbital plane ($z=0$) alongside the inner binary, defining key mass and length scales.

figures.caption: Figure 5: Mass loss rate of the donor star as a function of simulation time. The mass loss rate is calculated as the mass flux out of a spherical surface with a radius $r=2R_{d}$ centered about the donor. The negative sign denotes mass loss. Top: $\dot{M_{d}}$ for $a_{b}=0.15,\ 0.3,\ 0.6,\ 1.0$ (black, purple, pink, orange). The mass loss rate has a close-to-periodic variability, with the amplitude of the variablility increasing with the separation of the inner binary. For smaller separations $a_{b}$, the mass loss rate is close to zero, while for larger separations the mass loss rate is much larger. Bottom: We plot a zoomed in version to appreciate the subtle difference between $a_{b}=0.3$ (purple) and $a_{b}=0.15$ (black). All values are normalized by the average mass loss rate of a tertiary with a single accretor.
figures.label: Fig. 5
figures.physical_core: Time evolution and periodic variability of the donor star mass-loss rate $\dot{M}_d(t)$ (measured at $r=2R_d$) normalized to the single-accretor rate, revealing how increasing inner-binary separation $a_b \in [0.15, 1.0]$ dramatically amplifies the oscillation amplitude and orbit-averaged mass-loss rate via quadrupolar tidal forcing.

analysis.reason: The paper develops an interpretable Kernel Density Estimation and Direct Incidence Method applied to 14,855 RXTE LMXB spectra, establishing quantitative parameter boundaries that distinguish black hole from neutron star systems and identifying rare reflection-dominated states.
analysis.result: High-probability ($p > 0.99$) black hole systems occupy soft-state spectral regimes characterized by low blackbody temperature $kT_b < 1.05\,\mathrm{keV}$ (rank $< 0.25$) and high blackbody flux ratio $f_{\rm ratio} > 0.6$ (rank $> 0.88$), whereas neutron star systems exhibit harder emission with $kT_b > 1.6\,\mathrm{keV}$, photon index $\Gamma > 3$, $f_{\rm ratio} > 0.3$, and reduced $\chi^2 > 1.6$. Furthermore, the uniqueness metric successfully isolated the rare reflection-dominated state of neutron star EXO 1745-248 modeled by gravitational reflection (`relxillCp`).
analysis.reading_entry: III.3 Probability Distribution and most probable class characteristics
analysis.problem: Addressing the interpretability and black-box limitations of machine learning classifiers in X-ray astronomy while determining the physical spectral criteria that distinguish black hole from neutron star compact objects in low-mass X-ray binaries.
analysis.method: The Direct Incidence Method (DIM) discretizes $N_{\rm var}$ rank-ordered spectral variables into integer vectors $\vec{IV} \in \{0, \dots, N_{\rm bin}-1\}^{N_{\rm var}}$, evaluating class likelihood via KDE with a power-law kernel: $P_c(\vec{IV}) = \frac{1}{N_c} \sum_{\vec{IV'}} \frac{I_c(\vec{IV'})}{(D+s)^p}$, where $D = \sqrt{\sum_{j=1}^{N_{\rm var}} (IV'_j - IV_j)^2}$, $p=4$, and $s=0.5$. Outlier and unique spectra are identified via uniqueness metric $U(\vec{IV}) = \sum_{j=0}^{c_{\rm max}} \frac{1}{N_c} \sum_{\vec{IV'}} I_c(\vec{IV'}) D^{pd}$.
limits: Examining only the top vectors with the highest uniqueness values to select scientifically interesting sources introduces some arbitrariness, and the method relies on phenomenological fits rather than more complex physical Comptonization models due to statistical limitations.

analysis.problem: Constructing a coherent phase-connected timing model, characterizing binary orbital properties, identifying high-energy counterparts, and measuring interstellar propagation effects for the newly discovered eclipsing millisecond pulsar PSR J1840+1102.
analysis.method: Utilized uGMRT Band-4 ($550\text{--}750\,\mathrm{MHz}$) and Band-3 ($300\text{--}500\,\mathrm{MHz}$) coherent dedispersion timing observations reduced via PRESTO and TEMPO2. Adopted the ELL1 binary timing model using $T_{\mathrm{asc}} \simeq T_0 - \omega P_B / (2\pi)$ and Laplace-Lagrange parameters $\epsilon_1 = e\sin\omega$, $\epsilon_2 = e\cos\omega$ to avoid covariance in nearly circular orbits. Conducted Fermi-LAT weighted $H$-test pulsation searches, Shklovskii kinematic correction $\dot{P}_{\mathrm{shk}} = P\mu^2 d / c$, and MCMC profile deconvolution with an exponentially modified Gaussian to constrain scattering timescale $\tau(\nu) \propto \nu^{-\alpha}$.
assumptions: The binary orbit is sufficiently circular ($e \ll 1$) to justify the ELL1 timing approximation.
limits: The relatively high DM ($98.8\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$) increases susceptibility to turbulent interstellar medium variations and scattering jitter, limiting timing precision for PTA experiments.

analysis.reason: This work establishes critical methodological constraints on Fermi/GBM GRB spectral catalogue parameters, preventing relativistic jet and compact object population studies from confusing catalogue processing transitions and brightness-dependent fit statistics with intrinsic astrophysical evolution.
analysis.result: The core Comptonized (COMP) spectral shape is highly stable across the catalogue transition at GRB180712358, with effect sizes $|r_{\rm rb}| < 0.10$ across all ten physical parameters for the nominal $1024\text{ ms}$ long GRBs. Brighter bursts yield smaller formal parameter errors ($\gamma_{\rm br} = -0.667$ to $-0.750$) but systematically higher reported fit statistics ($b_{\rm br} = 0.169\text{--}0.439$) and stronger COMP-to-BAND improvements $\Delta S_{\rm CB} = S_{\rm COMP} - S_{\rm BAND} > 11.83$. BAND low-energy parameters $\alpha$ and $E_{\rm peak}$ remain reliable when error-bounded ($37.6\%\text{--}94.6\%$ usable), whereas the high-energy index $\beta$ is poorly constrained across the full catalogue (usable in only $1.9\%\text{--}37.5\%$ of bursts).
analysis.problem: Apparent multi-component GRB population clusters and temporal evolutions in the Fermi/GBM catalogue are frequently contaminated by instrumental selection effects, differing peak-flux integration timescales ($64\text{ ms}$ vs. $1024\text{ ms}$), and a discrete software/statistic transition at GRB180712358 (Castor C-STAT in period B vs. PSTAT in period A).
analysis.method: Statistical meta-analysis of $3337$ Fermi/GBM GRBs comparing empirical models (PLAW, COMP, BAND, SBPL) across catalogue periods A and B using standardized rank regression $Z_R(r_{\rm stat}) = b_{\rm br}Z_R(\log_{10}F) + b_\nu Z_R(\nu) + \epsilon$, bootstrap effect-size rank-biserial correlations $r_{\rm rb}$, and model selection thresholds $\Delta S_{\rm PC} = S_{\rm PLAW} - S_{\rm COMP} > 8.58$ and $\Delta S_{\rm CB} = S_{\rm COMP} - S_{\rm BAND} > 11.83$ based on Poisson deviance $C = 2\sum_i [\mu_i - n_i + n_i \ln(n_i / \mu_i)]$.
assumptions: Brighter Fermi/GBM spectra provide usable low-energy BAND parameters ($\alpha$, $E_{\rm peak}$), assuming empirical parameter precision can be decoupled from the high-energy slope $\beta$.
limits: A small formal parameter uncertainty does not guarantee that inferred parameters are model-independent, and BAND high-energy index $\beta$ is largely unconstrained (usable in only $1.9\%\text{--}37.5\%$ of bursts).

analysis.reason: This work presents the first high-resolution X-ray calorimetric 3D mapping of ejecta dynamics in Tycho's SNR with XRISM/Resolve, resolving Doppler splitting to disentangle velocity asymmetry from flux asymmetry.
analysis.result: Resolve unambiguously resolves Doppler splitting of K-shell lines into front (blueshifted) and rear (redshifted) shells. The line-of-sight velocities are $v_{\mathrm{front}}(\mathrm{Si}) = -3320 \pm 60\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$ and $v_{\mathrm{back}}(\mathrm{Si}) = +3920 \pm 100\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$ ($v_{\mathrm{front}}(\mathrm{S}) = -3250 \pm 50\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$, $v_{\mathrm{back}}(\mathrm{S}) = +3830 \pm 80\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$), showing a rear shell expansion $\sim 600\text{--}700\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$ faster than the front side (asymmetry $\sim 16\%$). Fe exhibits lower velocities ($v_{\mathrm{front}}(\mathrm{Fe}) = -2510\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$, $v_{\mathrm{back}}(\mathrm{Fe}) = +3330\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$) with velocity ratio $v_{\mathrm{Fe}}/v_{\mathrm{Si}} \approx 0.75$, consistent with projected radius ratio $R_{\mathrm{Fe}}/R_{\mathrm{Si}} \approx 0.85$. The front-side flux fraction $R = \frac{I_{\mathrm{front}}}{I_{\mathrm{front}} + I_{\mathrm{back}}}$ reaches $57\% \pm 1\%$ globally for Si and up to $70\%\text{--}80\%$ in the northeast.
analysis.problem: Previous CCD-based observations suffered from limited spectral resolution ($\nobreak >100\ \mathrm{eV}$), measuring only flux-weighted line-of-sight mean velocities that conflated intrinsic kinematic asymmetry with shell surface brightness asymmetry.
analysis.method: XRISM/Resolve $1.75\text{--}7.0\ \mathrm{keV}$ spectra across 5 pointings (149 pixels) were analyzed with Bayesian nested sampling (BXA/Sherpa/Xspec) using multi-Gaussian models over a synchrotron power law ($\Gamma \approx 2.75\text{--}2.83$). Line complexes of Si, S, Ar, Ca, and Fe were modeled with shared Doppler shifts per shell and global broadening ($\sigma \approx 16.5\text{--}23.7\ \mathrm{eV}$ at $2\ \mathrm{keV}$, corresponding to velocity dispersion $\Delta V_z \approx 2475\text{--}3555\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$), and synthesized into 3D velocity maps with Chandra proper motions ($V_{xy}$) assuming distance $d = 3.5\ \mathrm{kpc}$ via $V_{z,\mathrm{mean}} = V_{z,\mathrm{front}} \times \frac{I_{\mathrm{front}}}{I_{\mathrm{front}}+I_{\mathrm{back}}} + V_{z,\mathrm{back}} \times \left(1 - \frac{I_{\mathrm{front}}}{I_{\mathrm{front}}+I_{\mathrm{back}}}\right)$.
assumptions: Line complexes for intermediate-mass elements share an emissivity-weighted rest energy calculated assuming $kT_e = 1.2\ \mathrm{keV}$ and ionization timescale $n_e t = 2 \times 10^{10}\ \mathrm{cm^{-3}\ s}$.
citation_leads: 1 Introduction: “The expansion of the stellar material —the ejecta— drives a forward shock into the surrounding environment”
3.1 The Gaussian spectral models: “the Si, S, Ar, Ca and Fe K-lines appear split in blueshifted and redshifted components.”
4.1 Global fit: “about 3300 km s-1 (3320 km s-1 for Si and 3250 km s-1 for S) for the front shell, and about 3900 km s-1”
5.1 Comparison with previous CCD studies: “previous studies with CCD detectors measured the Doppler shift either by fitting the spectrum”
5.3 Element stratification: “We find a linear decrease in the velocity with increasing atomic number, from Si to Fe.”
Appendix A Rest Energy: “we adopt as the rest energy of each observed line of Si, S, Ar and Ca, the emissivity-weighted mean value”
analysis.research_progress: Establishes an empirical linear decrease in expansion velocity with increasing atomic number ($v_{\mathrm{ejecta}} \propto -Z$ from Si to Fe), confirming an unmixed, layered onion-like structure that rules out pure-deflagration explosion models and strongly favors delayed-detonation or double-detonation mechanisms.

figures.caption: Figure 12: Visualization in 3D velocity space summarizing our observations with XRISM/Resolve in this study. The dynamics appear asymmetrical, with the back side being faster than the front side. Fe is slower than Si and S. A flux asymmetry is observed: the front side is brighter (shown in blue in the figure) for Si, particularly in the North. This asymmetry is less pronounced for Fe, with more local enhancements (shown in local blue and red in the figure). The gray regions correspond to areas that are fainter along the line of sight.
figures.label: Fig. 12
figures.physical_core: Synthesizes the comprehensive 3D velocity-space morphology and ejecta dynamics of Tycho's SNR, highlighting the global kinematic asymmetry ($v_{\rm back} > v_{\rm front}$), elemental velocity stratification ($v_{\rm Fe} < v_{\rm Si}, v_{\rm S}$), and distinct line-of-sight flux asymmetries (with the front side up to twice as bright for Si).

figures.caption: Figure 10: 3D reconstruction in velocity space of the Si dynamics, for the three slices along the axis indicated in blue in the associated image (upper right). The velocity in the plane of the sky, V xy, is derived from proper motion measurements using Chandra data ( Godinaud et al., 2023 ). The Doppler velocities, V z, are measured in this analysis using XRISM/Resolve data. The red (back side) and blue (front side) points correspond to fits with two Gaussian components, while the green points represent single-Gaussian fits near the edges of the SNR. The black dashed circles correspond to a spherical 3D expansion with velocities of 3500 and 5000 km/s and are centered on 0 (the star marker).
figures.label: Fig. 10
figures.physical_core: Presents the 3D kinematic reconstruction in velocity space $(V_{xy}, V_z)$ for Si ejecta along three spatial slices, combining XRISM/Resolve line-of-sight Doppler velocities $V_z$ with Chandra proper-motion velocities $V_{xy}$ against spherical expansion models with $v_{\rm exp} = 3500\ \mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ and $5000\ \mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$.

analysis.reason: This paper presents a simulation-based Bayesian inference framework to constrain the universal gamma-ray luminosity function of millisecond pulsars (MSPs) in globular clusters directly from Fermi-LAT SEDs, providing important population constraints and methodology for high-energy compact object studies.
analysis.result: Using a baseline sample of 36 globular clusters, the universal log-normal MSP gamma-ray luminosity function yields median parameters and 68% credible intervals of $\log_{10}(L_{0}/\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}) = 33.4^{+0.4}_{-0.2}$ and $\sigma_{L} = 1.3^{+0.4}_{-0.5}$ (with mean luminosity $\langle L_{\gamma}\rangle = L_{0}\exp(\sigma_{L}^{2}/2)$). Inferred cluster gamma-ray MSP counts are $\log_{10}N_{\rm Ter5} = 1.8^{+0.2}_{-0.2}$ ($N_{\rm Ter5}\sim 70_{-24}^{+42}$), $\log_{10}N_{\rm 47\,Tuc} = 1.1^{+0.3}_{-0.2}$ ($N_{\rm 47\,Tuc}\sim 13$), and $\log_{10}N_{\rm NGC\,1851} = 0.7^{+0.3}_{-0.3}$ ($N_{\rm NGC\,1851}\sim 5$). Analyzing full SEDs rules out $\sigma_{L} < 0.5$ at $>3\sigma$ and prevents the overestimation of dispersion found when using integrated energy fluxes ($\sigma_{L} = 1.5^{+0.5}_{-0.4}$).

analysis.problem: Inferring the intrinsic gamma-ray luminosity function of MSPs in globular clusters previously relied on integrated gamma-ray fluxes paired with empirical multi-wavelength proxies (e.g., stellar encounter rates) to fix source counts, introducing strong model bias and parameter degeneracies. Furthermore, scaling conventional likelihood nested sampling to multiple clusters suffers from an intractable high-dimensional latent space.
analysis.method: The authors construct a forward simulator where MSP luminosities in each globular cluster are sampled from a universal log-normal luminosity function $\frac{\mathrm{d}N}{\mathrm{d}L_{\gamma}}=\frac{1}{L_{\gamma}\sigma_{L}\sqrt{2\pi}}\exp\left(-\frac{(\ln{L_{\gamma}}-\ln{L_{0}})^{2}}{2\sigma_{L}^{2}}\right)$ with individual spectra modeled by PLEC4, yielding individual flux $F_{{\rm MSP},c} = \frac{L_{c}}{4\pi d_{I}^{2}}$. They implement Simulation-Based Inference (SBI) using Neural Ratio Estimation (NRE, `swyft`) to perform amortized Bayesian inference directly on 0.1–100 GeV Fermi-LAT SEDs and phase-resolved ON/OFF spectra, marginalizing over unconstrained cluster MSP populations $N_{I}$ under log-uniform priors.
assumptions: MSPs across all globular clusters share a universal log-normal gamma-ray luminosity function parameterized by pivot luminosity $L_{0}$ and logarithmic width $\sigma_{L}$.
limits: Standard nested-sampling likelihood analysis scales exponentially with cluster count, preventing joint Bayesian inference beyond 3 clusters without SBI.

analysis.reason: This work provides the first relativistic calculation of dissipative tidal Love numbers of neutron stars arising from shear viscous heating, establishing a 4PN dissipative phase correction to binary neutron star gravitational waveforms.
analysis.result: The leading dissipative tidal response is governed by shear viscosity (with bulk viscosity suppressed in equilibrium tides due to $\Theta = 0$). For realistic equations of state (APR, SLy4, BSk24, DD2) at $1.4 M_\odot$ and redshifted temperature $T_\infty = 10^5\,\mathrm{K}$, the dimensionless dissipative Love number is $k_2^{(1)} \sim \mathcal{O}(10^{-5})$. Dissipative absorption enters the gravitational wave energy flux at relative 4PN order via $\mathcal{F}_{\rm tot} = \mathcal{F}_N (1 + \mathcal{A}_{\rm diss} v^8)$ with $\mathcal{A}_{\rm diss} = \frac{15}{16}\sum_{a=1}^2 (m_a/M)^4 C_a^{-6} k_{2,a}^{(1)} \sim 0.08\text{--}0.18$, accelerating the inspiral and producing a cumulative dephasing of $\delta\mathcal{N}_{\rm GW} = -\frac{5GM\mathcal{A}_{\rm diss}}{96\nu c^3}(f_f - f_i) \sim -10^{-3}\text{ to }-10^{-2}$ cycles over $20\text{--}1000\,\mathrm{Hz}$.
analysis.problem: How to consistently compute the leading dissipative tidal Love number $k_2^{(1)}$ of relativistic neutron stars from microscopic viscous dissipation, and quantify its secular impact on binary inspiral gravitational waveforms.
analysis.method: Formulates the dissipative response within worldline effective field theory (Schwinger-Keldysh in-in formalism) and matches the energy absorption rate $\dot{m}_{\rm EFT} = 2\lambda_2^{(1)}\dot{E}^{ij}\dot{E}_{ij}$ to the relativistic entropy-production volume integral $k_2^{(1)} = \frac{8\pi G}{15 R_*^6} \int_0^{R_*} \mathrm{d}r\, \frac{\eta(r)e^{-\Lambda/2}}{r^2} \mathcal{B}(r)$ evaluated on the static inviscid equilibrium tide, proving its exact equivalence to the odd-frequency metric perturbation problem $H_0(r,\omega) = H(r) + \mathrm{i}\omega R_* h(r)$.
assumptions: Away from equilibrium, the star is described by an imperfect fluid with stress-energy tensor governed by linear shear viscosity.
limits: Restricted to linear order in tidal frequency $\omega$ and linear order in shear viscosity $\eta$, neglecting nonlinear hydrodynamic instabilities and rotational coupling.

III Relativistic viscous heating: “Away from equilibrium, the star is described by an imperfect fluid with stress-energy tensor”
IV.2 Entropy-production integral: “This is the main result of the entropy-production method.”
IV.3 Metric response: “The vacuum perturbation equations contain no term linear in $\omega$.”

analysis.reason: This paper presents a targeted Fermi-GBM sub-threshold search for gamma-ray counterparts to 39 compact binary mergers with component masses exceeding the TOV limit from GWTC-5.0, providing observational constraints on prompt relativistic jet emission from binary black hole coalescences.
analysis.result: Among the 39 sub-threshold Fermi-GBM candidates identified across 161 super-TOV GW events ($M_1, M_2 \sim 7\text{--}100\,M_\odot$), none exhibit a prompt temporal offset consistent with relativistic jet launch ($t_{\rm delay} \sim 1.7\,\mathrm{s}$ as observed in GW170817). The smallest temporal separation is $\Delta t = 17\,\mathrm{min}\,17.976\,\mathrm{s}$, and candidates with high spatial overlap (e.g., GW240930_035959 with $95.4\%$ overlap) have excessive time delays ($\Delta t = 13\,\mathrm{h}\,19\,\mathrm{min}\,8.85\,\mathrm{s}$), ruling out genuine multi-messenger associations.
analysis.reading_entry: V.3 Progenitor Masses and the TOV Limit
analysis.problem: Investigating whether compact binary coalescence events with component masses exceeding the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff limit ($M_{\rm TOV} \approx 2.2\text{--}2.3\,M_\odot$) produce prompt sub-threshold gamma-ray emission, testing the standard theoretical expectation that vacuum binary black hole mergers lack matter to power relativistic jets.
analysis.method: Targeted search on Fermi-GBM continuous TTE data across 14 detectors (excluding $4\text{--}12\,\mathrm{keV}$) using the GTS pipeline over 8 timescales ($0.064\text{--}8.192\,\mathrm{s}$) to evaluate coherent log-likelihood ratios $\mathrm{LLR} = \ln[\mathcal{L}(D\mid S+B)/\mathcal{L}(D\mid B)]$, combined with systematic-corrected spatial overlap quantification $\mathcal{A}=\int_{4\pi} P_{\rm GRB}^{\rm sys}(\hat{n})P_{\rm GW}(\hat{n})\,d\Omega$ with LVK probability maps.
assumptions: Vacuum binary black hole (BBH) mergers lack baryonic tidal ejecta and surrounding matter necessary to launch prompt relativistic jets.
limits: Evaluated GW events are restricted to component masses $M_1, M_2 \sim 7\text{--}100\,M_\odot$ strictly above the neutron star TOV limit ($M_{\rm TOV} \approx 2.2\text{--}2.3\,M_\odot$).

analysis.reason: The paper presents a unified physical model bridging diamagnetic and magnetically threaded accretion discs around magnetized compact stars, deriving analytical torque profiles, inner disc radii, and thermal stability criteria directly applicable to transitional millisecond pulsars and X-ray pulsars.
analysis.result: Magnetic field penetration parameter $\eta$ modulates disc structure: for $\eta \sim 1$ in high accretion states, magnetic torques remove angular momentum, rendering the disc cooler, thinner, and less dense than standard $\alpha$-discs, with maximum hot disc radius $r_{\rm hot} = 2.2\times 10^{9}\,(\mu_{26}f_{200})^{0.63}M_{1.4}^{-0.2}(g/\omega^{2})^{0.31}\,{\rm cm}$. Torque reversal occurs stably at fastness $\omega_{\rm eq} \approx 0.88\text{--}0.95$, while in the dead disc limit ($\dot{M} \to 0$), magnetic extraction drives maximum spin-down rate $\dot{\nu} \approx -8.5 \times 10^{-14}\,{\rm s^{-2}}\,(g/\omega^2)$.
analysis.problem: Previous accretion disc models around magnetized stars relied on two conflicting extreme assumptions—either total magnetic screening (diamagnetic disc) or full magnetic threading—leaving the continuous transition in inner truncation radius $r_0$, angular momentum exchange, and vertical equilibrium unresolved.
analysis.method: Using a modified version of \texttt{AlphaDiSC}, the authors formulate a generalized thin-disc model incorporating penetration fraction $\eta \in [0, 1]$ ($B_z^{\rm in} = \eta B_z^{\rm dip}$), solve the vertical hydrostatic equilibrium $\frac{\mathrm{d}(P+b^{2}/8\pi)}{\mathrm{d}z}=-\rho\Omega_{\rm K}^{2}z(1+m)$, and establish a bridging formula for the inner radius $r_{0} = r_{\rm a}[\varepsilon_{0}^{7/2} + 2\eta^{2} (1-\omega) f_{\chi}]^{2/7}$.
assumptions: Thin accretion disc with Keplerian angular velocity approximation $|\delta_{\omega}| < 1$ across the active disc region
limits: The inner boundary conditions break down near corotation when $r_{\rm c}-r_{0} \lesssim z_{0}(r_{0})$, restricting solution validity to accretion rates $\dot{m} \gtrsim 3\eta^{2}f_{\chi}\,\delta_{0} \approx 0.03\text{--}0.2$

analysis.reason: This paper establishes a rigorous differentiable population synthesis and likelihood framework that accounts for binary survival and observational selection effects in supernova natal kick inferences, resolving discrepancies between isolated and binary neutron star kick distributions.
analysis.result: Neglecting binary survival selection severely biases the inferred supernova natal kicks: for a two-component model with true low-kick birth fraction $f_{\rm low} = 0.50$, surviving binaries are preferentially enriched, yielding an uncorrected mixture fraction of $0.5486 \pm 0.0131$ (a $3.71\sigma$ systematic bias), whereas selection-aware modeling recovers $0.5019 \pm 0.0132$. In single-progenitor mass–recoil experiments, ignoring survival selection underestimates true kick dispersions $\sigma_k = 100\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ and $300\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ to $88.9\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ and $189\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$, respectively. Combining $N_{\rm iso} = 3840$ isolated pulsars with $N_{\rm DNS} = 640$ double neutron stars constrains the core-collapse kick scale to $\sigma_{\ln\widetilde{w}_{\rm CC}} \simeq 0.077\sqrt{3840/N_{\rm iso}}$ (standard error $\sim 21\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$), effectively breaking the degeneracy between common-envelope efficiency $\alpha_{\rm CE}$ and kick magnitude. The reconstructed Galactic DNS merger rate across five classes is $25.33\,\mathrm{Myr}^{-1}$ (90% range $[11.63, 52.83]\,\mathrm{Myr}^{-1}$), but shifts up to $161.3\,\mathrm{Myr}^{-1}$ if the remaining radio lifetime of PSR J1906+0746 is reduced to $3\,\mathrm{Myr}$.
analysis.reading_entry: III Results: measurement capability and selection bias
analysis.problem: Asymmetries in core-collapse supernovae impart natal kicks $v_{\rm kick} \sim 100\text{--}1000\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ to neutron stars, which either disrupt binaries or reshape surviving orbits. Inferences from isolated pulsars favor high kicks while surviving binary pulsars favor low kicks; neglecting orbital survival and observational selection effects leads to severe systematic parameter biases and degenerate common-envelope prescriptions.
analysis.method: The authors developed `ad_sn_popsyn`, a differentiable two-supernova population synthesis engine implemented in pure 64-bit JAX. It tracks discrete evolutionary trajectories $x_{0}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{SN1}}s_{1}\xrightarrow{T_{\rm ins}}x_{1}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{SN2}}s_{2}$ using internal specific orbital energy $\varepsilon$ and squared specific angular momentum $h^2$, incorporates closed-form bound survival probabilities $P_{\rm bound}(w\mid r,v)=\frac{1}{2}[1+\mathrm{clip}_{[-1,1]}(\hat{c})]$, and evaluates the Poisson endpoint log-likelihood $\ln\mathcal{L}_{N}=\sum_{i}\ln K_{i}-N\ln\epsilon_{\rm DNS}$ along with Fisher information matrices $\widehat{\Gamma}_{N,ab}$ via forward-mode automatic differentiation and Rao-Blackwellization.

figures.caption: Figure 5: Evolution between the supernovae changes the binary that the second supernova acts on. Each point is one cosmic binary from our catalog that stays bound after the first supernova, colored by what happens before the second (counts in the legend). (a) Orbital separation just before the second supernova against that just after the first. (b) Mass of the star that explodes in the second supernova against its mass just after the first. The dashed line marks no change. Only detached binaries stay on it; mass transfer and common envelopes shrink the orbit by up to four orders of magnitude and strip the star that will explode. The catalog keeps only binaries that undergo two supernovae and favors those that merge, so the fractions are not those of all births. Generated with LLM assistance per Appendix C.

analysis.reason: This numerical relativity work demonstrates that tidal resonance locking of a counterrotating $f$-mode in an asymmetric binary neutron star system can excite late-inspiral orbital eccentricity, challenging the standard assumption of complete circularization before merger.
analysis.result: In an asymmetric BNS system ($m_1 = m_2 = 1.35\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$, $|\chi| = 0.5$, $\Lambda_1 = \Lambda_2 = 414.4$), single-sided tidal resonance during late inspiral induces an adjustment window of $\sim 9\text{--}17\,\mathrm{ms}$, causing the counterrotating NS spin $\hat{\chi}_2$ to decrease and driving the orbital eccentricity from $e \sim 7\times 10^{-4}$ linearly up to $e \sim 4\times 10^{-3}$, settling at $e \sim (3\text{--}4)\times 10^{-3}$.
analysis.problem: Isolated binary neutron star systems are conventionally assumed to fully circularize before reaching the ground-based gravitational-wave frequency band, but whether asymmetric tidal resonance of counterrotating $f$-modes can dynamically excite orbital eccentricity during late inspiral remained unproven.
analysis.method: Numerical relativity simulations using the BAM code with grid spacings $145\,\mathrm{m}$ (R192) and $217\,\mathrm{m}$ (R128) for an equal-mass BNS with SLy EOS, combined with a snowplow model based on the quasi-universal $f$-mode relation $\frac{\sigma_{i}^{\mathrm{u}}}{\sigma_{0}} = 1 + a_{1}^{\mathrm{u}}\left(\frac{|\Omega|}{\sigma_{0}}\right) + a_{2}^{\mathrm{u}}\left(\frac{|\Omega|}{\sigma_{0}}\right)^{2}$ ($a_1^{\mathrm{u}} = -0.193$, $a_2^{\mathrm{u}} = -0.0294$) yielding $\Omega(f_{\mathrm{GW}} \mid f_{\mathrm{GW}} > f_{\mathrm{lock,0}}) = \Omega_{0} - \frac{1}{a_{1}^{\mathrm{u}}}(f_{\mathrm{GW}} - f_{\mathrm{lock,0}})$.

Tidal resonance locking—: “reduction of the NS spin magnitude caused by the resonance leads to a shift of the counterrotating mode”
analysis.research_progress: Establishes that tidal resonance locking of counterrotating modes causes spin spindown and shifts mode frequency according to $\sigma_i^{\mathrm{u}} = \sigma_0 [1 + a_1^{\mathrm{u}}(|\Omega|/\sigma_0) + a_2^{\mathrm{u}}(|\Omega|/\sigma_0)^2]$, producing late-inspiral eccentricity $e \sim (3\text{--}4)\times 10^{-3}$ and demonstrating an intrinsic tidal mechanism for non-zero eccentricity without dynamical capture in dense star clusters.

analysis.reason: This work models polar shear ($s$) and interface ($i$) oscillation modes excited by neutron star crust elasticity, providing asteroseismic scaling relations to constrain nuclear incompressibility $K_0$ and symmetry energy slope $L$ relevant to resonant shattering precursors in compact binary mergers.
analysis.result: The radius-scaled shear mode frequencies $f_{s_i} R$ and mass-scaled interface mode frequencies $f_{i_i} M$ follow empirical universal relations parameterized by compactness $\chi \equiv (M/1.4M_\odot)/(R/12\ \mathrm{km})$, $K_0$, and $L$, largely independent of core equation of state stiffness. Spherical and cylindrical phases yield shear frequencies $f_s^{(\mathrm{SpCy})} \gtrsim 500\ \mathrm{Hz}$, while interface modes fall around $10-100\ \mathrm{Hz}$ with gravitational wave damping timescales $\tau_{\rm gw} \gtrsim 10^6\ \mathrm{s}$ for $s_1$ and $\tau_{\rm gw} > 10^8\ \mathrm{s}$ for $i_1$.
analysis.problem: Constraining uncertain nuclear matter parameters at saturation—namely incompressibility $K_0$ and symmetry energy slope $L$—using polar crustal oscillations ($s$- and $i$-modes) that penetrate into the stellar core, overcoming the limitation of torsional modes confined strictly to the crust.
analysis.method: Solves linear polar perturbations in a relativistic spherically symmetric metric $ds^{2}=-e^{2\Phi}dt^{2}+(1-2m(r)/r)^{-1}dr^{2}+r^{2}(d\theta^{2}+\sin^{2}\theta d\phi^{2})$ using the Cowling approximation $\delta(\nabla_{\mu}T^{\mu\nu})=0$. The crust employs the Oyamatsu-Iida EOS parameterized by $w=w_{0}+\frac{K_{0}}{2}u^{2}+[S_{0}+Lu]\delta^{2}$ with bcc lattice shear modulus $\mu_{\rm sp}=0.1194 n_{i}(Ze)^{2}/a$ and slab phase $\mu_{\rm sl}=0$, while the core uses a parameterized sound-speed EOS $p=\alpha(\varepsilon-\varepsilon_{t})+p_{t}$ with $\alpha=c_s^2$.

analysis.reason: The paper reports phase-resolved X-ray polarimetry of the persistent black hole binary LMC X-1 with IXPE, detecting low-energy orbital modulation and enhanced polarization at inferior conjunction that constrains disk-outflow geometries.
analysis.result: Phase-resolved IXPE polarimetry reveals orbital modulation statistically preferred over a constant model in the $2\text{--}8\,\mathrm{keV}$ ($F=10.0, p=0.0004$) and $2\text{--}3\,\mathrm{keV}$ ($F=7.53, p=0.0016$) bands, despite an orbit-averaged polarization degree of $\mathrm{PD} = (0.8 \pm 0.4)\%$ below $\mathrm{MDP}_{99} = 1.2\%$. At inferior conjunction ($\\phi \in [-0.1, 0.1]$), polarization increases significantly to $\mathrm{PD} = (3.4 \pm 0.8)\%$ with $\mathrm{PA} = (50 \pm 7)^\circ$ in $2\text{--}8\,\mathrm{keV}$ and $\mathrm{PD} = (4.2 \pm 1.1)\%$ with $\mathrm{PA} = (46 \pm 8)^\circ$ in $2\text{--}3\,\mathrm{keV}$, aligned with the ionization cone and jet axis ($\sim 45^\circ$). Dilution analysis using $P = P_{\mathrm{disk}} \times (F_{\mathrm{disk}} / F_{\mathrm{total}})$ yields intrinsic disk polarization of $P_{\mathrm{disk}} = (4.6 \pm 1.3)\%$ at $2\text{--}3\,\mathrm{keV}$ and $(2.3 \pm 1.3)\%$ at $3\text{--}8\,\mathrm{keV}$.
analysis.problem: Standard electron scattering in an optically thick accretion disk atmosphere with inclination $i = (36.4 \pm 1.9)^\circ$ predicts $\mathrm{PD} \sim 1.3\%$ oriented perpendicular to the disk normal ($\\mathrm{PA} \sim 135^\circ$). This fails to explain the observed enhanced polarization degree $\mathrm{PD} \sim 4\%$ parallel to the disk normal and ionization cone ($\\mathrm{PA} \approx 46^\circ$) at inferior conjunction, as well as the significant orbital phase modulation.
analysis.method: Coordinated timing, spectral, and polarimetric data reduction of IXPE ($2\text{--}8\,\mathrm{keV}$, $\sim 562\,\mathrm{ks}$), NICER ($1\text{--}10\,\mathrm{keV}$, $\sim 25\,\mathrm{ks}$), and NuSTAR ($3\text{--}40\,\mathrm{keV}$, $\sim 19\,\mathrm{ks}$) folded at $P = 3.90917\,\mathrm{days}$. Stokes parameter variations were fitted using $(Q/I)(t) = A_Q \cos(2\pi(t/P + \phi_0)) + C_Q$ and $(U/I)(t) = A_U \cos(2\pi(t/P + \phi_0) - \pi) + C_U$. Instrument cross-calibration was handled via the $\mathrm{MBPO}$ broken power-law model, and spectro-polarimetry used $\mathrm{MBPO} \times \mathrm{TBABS} \times (\mathrm{KERRBB} + \mathrm{NTHCOMP} + \mathrm{GAUSS})$.
assumptions: The binary parameters are fixed to black hole mass $M_{\mathrm{BH}} = (10.9 \pm 1.4)\,M_\odot$, companion mass $(32 \pm 3)\,M_\odot$, and orbital inclination $i = (36.4 \pm 1.9)^\circ$.

analysis.research_progress: Demonstrates an intrinsic self-arresting mechanism where counter-circulation from the vortex-depleted sector suppresses the boundary tangential velocity below $v_{\text{crit}}$, terminating the avalanche and establishing the scaling $\Delta\Omega_{c}^{*} \propto \Omega_{0} (I_{s}/I_{c})(d^{*}/R)^{2} \phi^{*}$.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Schematic of the superfluid flow in the presence of a sector devoid of vortices. Striped region indicates a vortex-free zone, with the rest of the container having a uniform distribution of vortices. Blue dashed arrow conveys the container’s direction of rotation. Blue and orange solid arrows specify the initial tangential flow and the effect of the sector, respectively. Purple arrowheads indicate the direction of flow on the contours of the vacated region due to the missing vortices. Left) Perturbation - A small sector near the boundary, of depth $d$ and opening angle $\phi$, is depleted of vortices, increasing the tangential flow at the tip. Right) Recapture - The sector is much larger than it was initially, now described by a depth $d^{*}$ and an opening angle $\phi^{*}$. The net flow at the tip is above critical, whereas that at the wall (where the forward arm of the sector meets the boundary) is exactly zero.
figures.label: Fig. 1
figures.physical_core: Schematic of the superfluid velocity field perturbation and recapture geometry caused by a vortex-free depletion sector of depth $d$ and opening angle $\phi$. As the vacated region expands to $(d^*, \phi^*)$, the induced counter-flow reduces the net tangential velocity at the boundary to zero, providing the physical mechanism that arrests the vortex exodus.

figures.caption: Figure 2: State of the vortex array, as observed in simulations, at the end of the exodus (left) and at the end of the entire event (right), arranged from top to bottom, increasing in $v_{\text{crit}}$ (30, 60, 90). Black dots represent vortices. Pinning sites, more numerous than the vortices, are not shown. In all the cases, the radius of the container R=10. The opening angle $\phi^{*}$ and the depth $d^{*}$ recorded at the end of exodus increases with $v_{\text{crit}}$. However, the total depth of the disturbance, apparent at the end of the entire event, is seen to reduce with $v_{\text{crit}}$.
figures.label: Fig. 2
figures.physical_core: Numerical simulation snapshots of the quantized vortex array during spinning-down, comparing the state at the end of the exodus against the end of the complete event across critical unpinning velocities $v_{\text{crit}} \in \{30, 60, 90\}$. It demonstrates that the depletion sector dimensions $(d^*, \phi^*)$ grow with $v_{\text{crit}}$, while the total disturbance depth contracts.

key_highlights.result: The $\mu$TDE produces two accretion flares: a prompt fallback onto the stellar BH with peak rate $\approx 0.5\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{day}^{-1}$ (duration of hours to days) and a delayed slower return onto the MBH peaking at $\approx 50\,\mathrm{days}$ with a rate $\sim 3$ orders of magnitude lower.
